The paper starts with a deterministic multi-scale Lagrangian particle system, where the Lagrangian flow map is split into a slow mean component g_bar and a rapidly fluctuating component g'.
The rapidly fluctuating vector displacement field is defined as ζ = g' - Id, where ε << 1 is the scale separation parameter.
The full Lagrangian trajectory is given by q(l,t) = g_bar(l,t) + ζ(q_bar(l,t),t/ε), where q_bar is the trajectory of the slow mean component.
The centering condition requires that the mean of the fluctuating deviations ζ is small when pulled back to the mean flow, i.e., ⟨(Id+∇ζ)^(-1) ∂_t ζ⟩ = 0.
Homogenization theory is applied to the deterministic multi-scale Lagrangian system, assuming sufficiently chaotic fast dynamics for the fluctuations.

The homogenization analysis shows that the slow dynamics of the Lagrangian particle system is described by a stochastic differential equation dQ_bar = U_bar(Q_bar)dt + σ(Q_bar)dW, where U_bar and σ are the derived drift and diffusion terms.
The drift term U_bar has two contributions: the average of the full velocity over the fluctuations, and an additional term arising from the statistics of the fluctuation time-derivative.
The diffusion tensor σ σ^T depends on the autocorrelation function of the fast fluctuating flow map g'.
The derived stochastic Lagrangian dynamics matches the structure of the stochastic vector field Ansatz used in the previous variational approach [8, 3].
To compute the EOF eigenvectors ξ_i for the stochastic model, one can analyze time series of Lagrangian displacement vectors ζ obtained from high-resolution simulations or observational data.
The performance of the stochastic model constructed this way is currently being evaluated using data assimilation algorithms.
